subject: Post-term usage reconciliation & credit ladder proposal
body:
From: Jordan Hale <j.hale@olivetech.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@olivetech.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-term usage reconciliation & credit ladder proposal

Thanks Laura — appreciate the breakdown. Two quick items: 1) the spike in March was due to an integration test that accidentally hit prod for 24 hours, which Procurement is tracking internally; 2) we need the final dollar amount and suggested path to settle before the end of May so we can clear it through accounts payable. Can you confirm whether Redwood can offer any amortized credit instead of a single invoice?

— Jordan
Senior Platform Engineer, OliveTech

-----Original Message-----
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Hale <j.hale@olivetech.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Post-term usage reconciliation & credit ladder proposal

Jordan — thanks again for the call earlier. Per our notes, attached is the usage export for March–April and two settlement options: 1) one-time reconciliation invoice for the incremental overage; or 2) a credit ladder where we convert 50% of the invoice into a refundable credit applied over the next 3 monthly bills (33% / 33% / 34%).

High-level numbers (rounded):
- Committed capacity (Q1–Q2 term): 5M tokens/month
- Observed peak month (March): 12.4M tokens
- Billed usage that exceeded commit (net): 9.6M tokens over period
- Proposed one-time invoice (list rate): $38,400
- Proposed credit-ladder (50% convert): $19,200 credit; immediate invoice $19,200 then credits applied 1/3 months

We can also consider a 90-day amnesty window where we waive the first $5k of one-time fees if OliveTech accepts the three-month ladder and an amendment to increase committed capacity to 8M tokens/month for the next 12 months (with a 6% discount on overage rate). That preserves predictability for both sides.

Attachments: olive_march_april_usage_breakdown.csv, credit-ladder-proposal.xlsx, amendment-draft-v2.pdf

Please review and advise which option Procurement prefers — if you want, Ben (Finance) and Marcus (CS) can jump on a short call to finalize PO wording and the amendment.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

-----Original Message-----
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-term usage reconciliation & credit ladder proposal

Laura — saw the numbers. Finance prefers the simplest path (one-time invoice) for recognition reasons, but we can accommodate the ladder if OliveTech signs the amendment now and provides a PO that references the amortization schedule. If they want the amnesty waiver, it needs an approval code from Sales Leadership.

Tentative accounting treatment: immediate revenue on the invoiced portion; deferred revenue on the credit that gets consumed over the next 3 months. We’ll need the signed amendment PDF (amendment-draft-v2.pdf) and a PO tied to the account to process the credit entries.

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

-----Original Message-----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Hale <j.hale@olivetech.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-term usage reconciliation & credit ladder proposal

Jordan — quick note from CS side: if OliveTech agrees to the capacity increase to 8M tokens/mo and the 6% overage discount, we will provide a one-time onboarding credit of 200k prompt tokens to help smooth the transition and avoid another spike. That onboarding credit would be consumed first before overages are billed. Also happy to coordinate the technical guardrails to prevent accidental prod hits.

Marcus Lin
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

-----Original Message-----
From: Jordan Hale <j.hale@olivetech.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@olivetech.com, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-term usage reconciliation & credit ladder proposal

Thanks Marcus — the onboarding token credit is a helpful concession. Procurement has one ask: any amortization schedule must map to invoice line items we can approve; DocuSign signatures are preferred for the amendment. Laura — can you produce a redlined amendment with the ladder schedule embedded, and a corresponding invoice draft we can sign/approve? Also confirm whether the waived $5k amnesty requires internal approval.

— Jordan

-----Original Message-----
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Hale <j.hale@olivetech.com>, procurement@olivetech.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-term usage reconciliation & credit ladder proposal

Jordan / Procurement team — next steps below: 
1) I attached amendment-draft-v2.pdf with the ladder language and the amortization table embedded (see page 2). Please review and confirm the PO line references you need; if you send the PO number we’ll generate the invoice templates to match.
2) Amnesty waiver: I have Sales Leadership (Evelyn) on copy — Evelyn can approve the $5k goodwill waiver for this case if OliveTech signs the amendment and provides PO within 5 business days.
3) If you prefer the single invoice, we’ll issue $38,400 immediately and apply the onboarding 200k token credit against future bills per Marcus’s note.

If Procurement can route the PO to procurement@redwood.ai with invoice line references (for example: OLIVE-INV-TRUEUP-202705), we’ll generate the DocuSign packet and payment instructions same day.

I’ll stand by for the PO or a calendar invite for a 20-min call if you want to finalize live.

Thanks — Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments referenced:
- olive_march_april_usage_breakdown.csv (CSV, 48KB)
- credit-ladder-proposal.xlsx (XLSX, 22KB)
- amendment-draft-v2.pdf (PDF, 68KB)
